name: App connections rebuilt by every product
problem: Many products rebuild each app connection (calendar, drive, notes, chat) with their own screen, storage and tool code, so a new app costs code in every layer and often arrives months after hubs list it.
who_has_it: Teams whose users want their own apps connected to an AI.
why_it_matters: Users get the apps a team had time to wire, not the apps they use, and each connection is a new place for credentials to leak.
why_hard: Each app has its own sign-in, scopes and tools, and a user's credentials must never reach another user's turns.
existing_attempts: Hand-written adapters per app; integration hubs that expose many apps as MCP tools but leave the connect screen, credential storage and consent to each product.

name: One integration needs several hubs
problem: An app connection (a calendar, a drive, a chat) is often served better by several hubs combined than by any one, but a product usually wires a single hub and hand-writes the rest.
who_has_it: Teams whose users connect their own apps to an AI.
why_it_matters: The user gets the part of the app one hub exposes, and every gap becomes new code in the product.
why_hard: Each hub has its own sign-in, scopes and tools, so combining them means mapping which hub serves which action, and that mapping is usually written by hand.
existing_attempts: One integration hub per product, and hand-written adapters for what it misses.

name: Enduring integrations unused
problem: A system often already has enduring integrations, such as its own AI tool registry, LLM platform and guardrails, and the AI cannot reach them or does not use them.
who_has_it: Teams that run AI inside an enterprise system.
why_it_matters: Duplicate tools and unguarded calls appear beside the ones the system already governs.
why_hard: Each system declares its integrations in its own way.
